The '''M<sub>22</sub> graph''', also called the '''Mesner graph''' or '''Witt graph''',<ref name="mesner"/><ref name="mesner2"/><ref name="mesner3"/><ref name=ekr>{{citation
 | last1 = Godsil | first1 = Christopher | author1-link = Chris Godsil
 | last2 = Meagher | first2 = Karen
 | contribution = Section 5.4: The Witt graph
 | isbn = 9781107128446
 | pages = 94–96
 | publisher = Cambridge University Press
 | series = Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics
 | title = Erdős–Ko–Rado Theorems: Algebraic Approaches
 | url = https://www.cambridge.org/ht/academic/subjects/mathematics/discrete-mathematics-information-theory-and-coding/erdoskorado-theorems-algebraic-approaches
 | year = 2015}}</ref> is the unique [[strongly regular graph]] with parameters (77, 16, 0, 4).<ref name="tnl">[[Brouwer, Andries E.]] “M<sub>22</sub> Graph.” [[Technische Universiteit Eindhoven]], http://www.win.tue.nl/~aeb/graphs/M22.html. Accessed 29 May 2018.</ref> It is constructed from the [[Steiner system]] (3, 6, 22) by representing its 77 blocks as vertices and joining two vertices [[iff]] they have no terms in common, or by deleting a vertex and its neighbors from the [[Higman–Sims graph]].<ref name="mathworld">Weisstein, Eric W. “M22 Graph.” MathWorld, http://mathworld.wolfram.com/M22Graph.html. Accessed 29 May 2018.</ref><ref name="ucdenver">Vis, Timothy. “The Higman–Sims Graph.” University of Colorado Denver, http://math.ucdenver.edu/~wcherowi/courses/m6023/tim.pdf. Accessed 29 May 2018.</ref>

For any term, the family of blocks that contain that term forms an [[independent set (graph theory)|independent set]] in this graph, with 21 vertices. In a result analogous to the [[Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem]] (which can be formulated in terms of independent sets in [[Kneser graph]]s), these are the unique [[maximum independent set]]s in this graph.<ref name=ekr/>

It is one of seven known [[triangle-free]] strongly regular graphs.<ref>Weisstein, Eric W. “Strongly Regular Graph.” From Wolfram MathWorld, mathworld.wolfram.com/StronglyRegularGraph.html.</ref> Its [[graph spectrum]] is (−6)<sup>21</sup>2<sup>55</sup>16<sup>1</sup>,<ref name="mathworld"/> and its [[automorphism group]] is the [[Mathieu group M22]].<ref name="tnl"/>
